chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Yaqoub ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not prohibit wine (khamr) because of its name, but He prohibited it because of its consequence/effect. So whatever produces the effect of wine, it is wine.

key_terms.الْخَمْرُ: Wine; specifically refers to the intoxicating drink, used here as the archetype for all intoxicants.
key_terms.فَمَا فَعَلَ فِعْلَ الْخَمْرِ: So whatever produces the effect of wine; the legal criterion for classifying other substances as wine.
key_terms.لِعَاقِبَتِهَا: Because of its consequence/effect; refers to the intoxicating property that causes the prohibition.

ai.seo_question: What is the basis for prohibiting wine and other intoxicants in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi establishes 'illa al-khamr' (the cause of prohibition) as intoxication rather than the specific grape origin, allowing for the extension of the ruling to all intoxicants via qiyas. This principle is foundational for classifying modern substances like alcohol and drugs under the same legal category, emphasizing the functional consequence over the material substance.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Yaqoub Bin Yaqteen, from his brother Ali Bin Yaqteen, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High did not Prohibit the wine for its name, but Prohibited it due to its consequences. So whatever affects with the effect of the wine, so it is (classified as) wine’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from Ya’qub ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother Ali ibn Yaqtin who has said the following: “Abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Allah, the most Blessed, the most High, has not made wine unlawful because of its name. He has made it unlawful because of its consequences, therefore, whatever, works as wine does, it then is wine.’”
